Subject: Pre-deploy questions: operator runbook + KMS routing

Hi Kimberly / Jonas —

Thanks again for the workshop this morning. We're drafting our cutover checklist for the private VPC deployment and have a couple of tight questions before we finalize:

1) Operator runbook: can you share the latest draft that covers day-0 / day-1 / day-30 run actions for the control-plane and data-plane separation? We're particularly interested in rollback steps if the gateway attachment fails.

2) KMS routing: our security team needs a concrete routing pattern for customer-managed KMS traffic (to avoid unintended egress). Do you recommend in-place proxying (customer KMS endpoint routed through the onprem egress) or a dedicated outbound NAT with KMS allowlist? Any sample iptables/route examples would be super-helpful.

I've attached a short doc with our questions (edgeops-kms-questions.pdf). Can you respond with a runbook draft and any sample configs we can adapt? If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical alignment.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Senior SRE, EdgeOps Solutions

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pre-deploy questions: operator runbook + KMS routing

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached the current operator runbook draft for private VPC (vpc-operator-runbook-draft.md). High-level answers below and a short appendix in the runbook with sample iptables / NAT rules.

- Operator runbook: the doc includes sections for control-plane actions (certificate propagation, control-plane health checks, API proxy failover) and data-plane actions (node admission, egress policy checks, KV cache warm-up). The rollback section recommends an automatic control-plane rollback + manual data-plane drain if the attachment step fails. See the "Deployment failure -> rollback" checklist (page 6).

- KMS routing: for customer-managed keys we recommend a dedicated outbound NAT with a small allowlist to minimize proxy state and avoid TLS termination. Pattern:
  * Customer KMS endpoint -> egress NAT with static SNAT -> allowed on customer-approved KMS IPs
  * Use route-based ACLs on the edge router to limit destinations by IP range

We deliberately avoid TLS-intercept proxies for KMS because customers generally require end-to-end TLS to their KMS provider for attestation. The attached kms-routing-examples.txt contains an example for a linux host ip rule set and a sample NAT pool mapping for the egress gateway.

Open questions for you:
- Can you confirm whether EdgeOps will accept a static outbound SNAT IP range or do you require per-tenant dedicated IPs?
- Are there any corporate firewalls that would block SNATed traffic to your KMS provider (we can suggest an alternate proxy pattern if necessary).

If those answers look good, let's sync on a short call. I'm available Thu 11/19 09:30-10:30 PT or 2:00-3:00 PT.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 10:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> We deliberately avoid TLS-intercept proxies for KMS because customers generally require end-to-end TLS to their KMS provider for attestation.

Tom —

Quick technical note from my side (adding to the runbook appendix): if you go the SNAT path, make sure the egress gateway preserves client source port entropy for long-lived TLS connections (some cloud NATs rewrite ports aggressively which breaks some HSM client libraries). Example iptables snippet we tested:

  # iptables rules for SNAT pool
  iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.10.0.0/16 -d 35.200.0.0/16 -j SNAT --to-source 198.51.100.10-198.51.100.14

And a small keepalive tweak for the KMS client: set TCP_KEEPINTVL=30 and TCP_KEEPIDLE=120 to avoid idle tear-downs.

Also calling out: control-plane health checks should include a KV-cache checksum after migration to ensure the inference runtime doesn't diverge. I added that to the day-1 validation checklist in the runbook.

Happy to run through the snippet on the call.

—Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
